sentences.text: The Medication Order Gateway is called Morrowglass in this concept.
The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler is called Bluejay in this concept.
The Pharmacy Technician is called Copperfield in this concept.
The Medication Order Gateway accepts medication orders from authorized clinical systems and records their arrival times.
It checks required order fields, patient identifiers, medication codes, quantities, and destination details before routing an order for pharmacy review.
The gateway flags missing data, duplicate submissions, and changes that conflict with the active order record.
The Medication Order Gateway produces the Order Reconciliation Snapshot for documenting detected order discrepancies.
The Pharmacy Verification Station displays queued orders and their validation results for review.
The Clinical Pharmacist evaluates clinical appropriateness, dose limits, allergies, and relevant interactions before approving an order.
The Pharmacy Technician investigates administrative discrepancies and requests clarification through approved clinical channels.
Unresolved discrepancies keep an order from advancing to preparation.
The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot prepares only orders that have passed the required review and authorization checks.
The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler maintains refrigerated medications within the facility's approved temperature range.
Continuous sensors record temperature readings and report excursions or loss of monitoring connectivity.
The Pharmacy Technician checks the cooler's status and confirms that refrigerated stock remains within handling limits before use.
The Pharmacy Technician produces the Cold Chain Handoff Card to document custody and handling conditions.
When an excursion occurs, affected stock is segregated pending assessment and disposition by authorized pharmacy staff.
Temperature records are retained with timestamps so reviewers can establish the duration and extent of an excursion.
The Clinical Pharmacist determines whether affected medication remains suitable for dispensing under approved procedures.
The Pharmacy Technician checks packaging, product identity, lot details, and expiry information during routine stock handling.
The Medication Safety Officer reviews patterns of discrepancies and handling events for potential safety concerns.
The Medication Safety Officer produces the Diversion Review Packet when a diversion concern requires documented review.
The Pharmacy Verification Station preserves review decisions and order status changes in an auditable record.
Orders remain unavailable for dispensing until required checks are complete and their status is authorized.
